column1: # Hebrew for the "Write in ..." tool (scribe.js); built into scribe-langs.js by scripts/make-scribe.ps1.
# Values are the usual scholarly transliteration of the letters (ʾ b g d h w z ḥ ṭ y k l m n s ʿ p ṣ q r š t); the
# typed forms after them are the ASCII ways to reach them. rules=hebrew: short a and e inside a word are not written,
# i becomes yod and o, u vav, a word-initial vowel takes alef, a final a or e takes he, doubled letters are written
# once, and the five letters with final forms take them at the end of a word. "Vowel marks" adds the niqqud instead.

column4: Hebrew is written from right to left with 22 letters, all of them consonants; the vowels were added later as dots and dashes (niqqud).

column2: The “square” letters, taken over from the Aramaic script after the Babylonian exile (6th century BCE) and still used today.

Type as it sounds: sh for ש, ch for ח, ts for צ, ' for א and ` for ע. Short a and e inside a word are left out; i becomes י and o or u become ו, as in many Hebrew spellings; final letters (ך ם ן ף ץ) appear by themselves. The line under the letters spells out what is written.

column4: alef · silent, or a catch in the throat
vav · v (anciently w); also o and u
ayin · a sound from deep in the throat
final kaf · kaf at the end of a word
final mem · mem at the end of a word
final nun · nun at the end of a word
final pe · pe at the end of a word
final tsadi · tsadi at the end of a word
sheva · a short e, or no vowel
dagesh · a doubled or hard letter

column3: Shalom: peace, and also hello and goodbye
Tikkun olam: “repairing the world”, a phrase found in the Mishnah
Bereshit: “in the beginning”, the first word of the Bible and the Hebrew name of Genesis

column2: The older Hebrew letters, close to the Phoenician alphabet, used by the kingdoms of Israel and Judah from about the 10th century BCE.
The same letters in their older shapes, with no final forms and a dot between words, as on the Siloam inscription. Type as for Hebrew: sh, ch, ts, ' and `.

column4: alef · silent, or a catch in the throat
waw · w; also o and u
ayin · a sound from deep in the throat

column3: “And this was the matter of the tunnel”: the Siloam inscription, cut in Hezekiah’s tunnel in Jerusalem around 700 BCE
